about: The folk of the hamlets: the world’s set pieces. Each hamlet gets three or four (a seller, a keeper of something, and one or two more), made from a name, a job and the hamlet’s age (old: there before the road; new: went up after the lantern woke). They can’t be befriended or recruited. A job with a post (the well, the stall, a home) stands beside it. They say one thing at a time, and only what they would say: plain, deadpan, no stage directions.

ages.old: An old place. It was here before the road.
ages.new: A new place. It went up after the lantern woke.

roles.title: keeps the well
any: The well is fine. I check it every hour. It has never not been fine.
People drop coins in. I take them out. It evens up.
old: This well is older than the road. The road is sensitive about it.
new: We dug it in the spring. We hit water on the second day. Nobody was more surprised than the water.
roles.cool: That was the tree by the well. It kept the bucket company. I’ll check on the bucket.
roles.warm: You again. I’ve told the well about you. It took it well.

roles.title: bakes
any: There is bread. There is always bread. I don’t know how to stop.
I made too many loaves again. Take one. Take four.
old: This oven was my grandmother’s. She is still in charge of it. She has been gone nine years.
new: The oven is new. It hasn’t burned anything yet. I don’t trust it.
roles.cool: There’s bread. You can’t have any today. That was a good tree.
roles.warm: I kept you the end of a loaf. It’s the best bit. Don’t tell the middle.

roles.title: lights the lamps
any: I light them at dusk. Then I put them out at dawn. It is a living.
One lamp won’t light. I talk to it. It hasn’t helped.
old: These lamps were here before the Hush. I only inherited the ladder.
new: We put the lamps up last month. We are very proud of both of them.
roles.cool: I hung a lamp on that tree. I’ll hang it on the stump. It’s lower. I’ve noted my feelings.
roles.warm: I leave one lit for you now. Don’t make a thing of it.

roles.title: minds the goats
any: There are six goats. I count seven most days. I have stopped asking.
The goats eat the laundry. We have less laundry now. It works out.
old: My family has minded these goats for a hundred years. The goats don’t seem grateful.
new: We brought the goats with us. They chose the spot. We built round them.
roles.cool: The goats saw you do it. I can’t speak for them. One of them is writing something.
roles.warm: The goats know your walk. Six of them do. The seventh says it doesn’t.

roles.title: watches the road
any: Nobody has come down this road today except you. I have written that down.
I watch the road. It doesn’t do much. I watch it anyway.
old: I’ve stood here thirty years. A great many people have walked past. Two of them stopped.
new: They gave me the job because I was already standing here.
roles.cool: One tree down, your side of the road. I’ve written it up. I underlined your name.
roles.warm: You’ve come up this road three times. I don’t write you down any more. I just nod.

roles.title: fishes
any: I haven’t caught anything. I’ve been here since morning. I’m not in a hurry.
The fish know me. That’s the problem.
old: My father fished this water. He didn’t catch anything either. It’s a family trade.
new: I was told there were fish here. I’m still looking into it.
roles.cool: You cut the tree I sit under. Now I sit under nothing. The fish can see me.
roles.warm: Sit. You don’t scare the fish. Nothing does. But sit.

roles.title: is seven
any: I’m seven. I’m in charge of the puddle.
I found a rock. You can look at it. You can’t have it.
old: My house is the old one. It leans. I lean too, so it looks straight.
new: We’re new. I have been here two weeks. I know where everything is.
roles.cool: You cut down the tree. It was the climbing one. I’m frowning. Look.
roles.warm: You’re back. I told the puddle. It’s your puddle too now. A bit of it.

roles.title: remembers when
any: I remember when this was all fields. It is still mostly fields.
Sit down if you want. I was going to anyway.
old: I was born in that house. I’ve been meaning to leave.
new: I’m too old to start a village. I started one anyway.
roles.cool: That tree was planted the year I was born. I didn’t much care for it. All the same.
roles.warm: I remember when you were new here. It was last week. Still.

roles.title: builds
any: I’m building a fence. It’s to keep the other fence in.
Measure twice, cut once. I measured four times. I haven’t cut anything.
old: I mend what my father built. He built it badly. It keeps me in work.
new: Everything here is new. I made most of it. Don’t lean on anything yet.
roles.cool: You felled it badly. I’d have felled it badly too, but I’d have asked.
roles.warm: I made you a peg by the door. It’s for a hat. Get a hat.

roles.title: sells things
any: I sell rope, lamp oil and one hat. The hat is not for sale.
Business is slow. You are the business.
old: This stall has been in the family for six generations. We have sold the same rope twice.
new: I opened yesterday. You are my second customer. The first was me.
roles.cool: Shut. On account of the tree. I’d have sold you the axe. That makes it worse.
roles.warm: Regular’s price for you. It’s the same price. But I say it differently.
